label: first-summary-v1
summary: One companion, one facility, one band, scalar summary measurements.

conventions.name: sky_basis
conventions.statement: Right-handed, star-centred (east, north, away) frame in AU; row 2 is positive away from the observer.

conventions.name: east_offset
conventions.statement: The east offset is Delta alpha cos(delta): the declination factor is already applied and is never applied again.

conventions.name: node
conventions.statement: The longitude of the ascending node is measured from north through east; the ascending node is the sky-plane crossing where the planet moves away from the observer.

conventions.name: position_angle
conventions.statement: Position angle increases with time for inclinations below 90 degrees.

conventions.name: inclination
conventions.statement: Inclination lies in [0, pi], isotropic in the prior (cos i uniform in [-1, 1]).

conventions.name: phase_angle
conventions.statement: Standard star-planet-observer phase angle with cos(beta) = z / r and z away: 0 at superior conjunction (full phase), pi at inferior conjunction. No supplement conversion is applied anywhere.

conventions.name: argument_of_periastron
conventions.statement: The planet's argument of periastron is the radial-velocity (stellar) argument of periastron plus 180 degrees.

conventions.name: time_scale
conventions.statement: Absolute epochs are Julian Dates in TDB as float64; MJD = JD - 2400000.5.

conventions.name: tick
conventions.statement: One tick is 1 ms; tick 0 of a study is the context's origin epoch, held as an integer number of ticks from J2000.0 (JD 2451545.0 TDB).

conventions.name: intervals
conventions.statement: A record's start and end ticks delimit occupancy (settling, then science). The science interval is [start + settle, end]; for a complete visit it is the last exposure_ticks of the occupancy.

conventions.name: record_epoch
conventions.statement: The record epoch is the midpoint of the science interval.

conventions.name: certification
conventions.statement: Before acquisition, every admissible executed start in [planned_start, planned_start + max_delay] must keep the whole occupied interval inside the keepout window and the response support; at run time a science interval outside the certified window gives valid_science = 0.

conventions.name: keepout
conventions.statement: Sun keepout 45 to 180 degrees, Earth keepout 0 to 180 degrees (inactive), both passed explicitly to orbix.

conventions.name: response_origin
conventions.statement: Header centre N/2 is zero-based pixel-centre index N/2 - 0.5 (127.5 on a 256 grid) for every azimuthal operation.

conventions.name: leakage_operator
conventions.statement: Stellar leakage in the aperture is the azimuthal-mean intensity per pixel divided by 0.25^2 and multiplied by the core area in (lambda/D)^2.

conventions.name: dqe
conventions.statement: dQE is an explicit survival fraction, neutral 1.0, always passed; QE is applied exactly once.

conventions.name: background_multiplier
conventions.statement: Background variance multiplier k = 1 (one roll, no differencing, known mean subtracted), passed explicitly.

conventions.name: systematic_floor
conventions.statement: The systematic noise floor is off in the planner and the law (ppfact infinite).

conventions.name: thermal
conventions.statement: Thermal emission is off (eps_warm_T_cold = 0); the telescope temperature is inert.

conventions.name: exozodi
conventions.statement: Fexozodi at 1 AU = n_ez x one-zodi surface brightness x (L / Lsun), with n_ez = 3 passed explicitly.

conventions.name: detection
conventions.statement: Detection is the event counts >= 5 limit_counts; a null is the complementary event at a realized science duration t > 0.

conventions.name: cadence
conventions.statement: Fixed frames with integer frame counts; until the finite-duration variance API exists the legacy photon-counting cadence runs and every row says so.

time.study_epoch_note: 2030-01-01 00:00 TDB, a declared fixture choice for the start of the first campaign

targets.name: 47 UMa
targets.source: NASA ExEP Mission Star List for HWO (Mamajek and Stapelfeldt 2024, arXiv:2402.12414), row HIP 53721 as served by the NASA Exoplanet Archive table di_stars_exep; distance from the Gaia DR3 parallax 72.0070 mas

planet.name: 47 UMa b
planet.source: Gregory and Fischer (2010), MNRAS 403, 731 (arXiv:1003.5549), Table 6 (final three-planet model from the combined Lick, HET and HJS data; medians, planet 1); periastron passage listed as JD - 2440000 = 11917; omega is the stellar argument of periastron of the radial-velocity model

declared.note: Not measured. Inclination 60 degrees is the median of an isotropic inclination prior; the node is a convention choice; the radius is the IAU 2015 nominal Jovian equatorial radius; the albedo is a planning value. Nominal values enter the plan only; the world source draws radius and albedo from the prior.

prior.note: photomancy's orbit prior; the period range is the published period plus or minus three standard deviations, the other ranges are photomancy's model defaults

targets.name: solar twin at 10 pc
targets.source: Synthetic fixture: a solar twin at 10 pc on the celestial equator at RA 0 (ecliptic latitude 0); Teff is the IAU 2015 nominal solar effective temperature

planet.name: Earth twin
planet.source: Synthetic fixture: an Earth twin on a circular one-year orbit

declared.note: Synthetic; the radius is the nominal Earth equatorial radius and the albedo a planning value.

prior.note: photomancy's orbit prior with a period range around one year

payload_columns.name: time_d
payload_columns.measure: Julian Date (TDB) of the science-interval midpoint

payload_columns.name: detected
payload_columns.sign: flag: 1 detection, 0 null or no science

payload_columns.name: counts
payload_columns.sign: signed (noise can make it negative); 0 and unread unless detected = 1
payload_columns.measure: measured planet counts integrated over the band and the science interval, known background mean subtracted

payload_columns.name: limit_counts
payload_columns.measure: planet-free noise standard deviation from the nominal backgrounds and the detector variance at the realized science duration

payload_columns.name: snr
payload_columns.measure: counts divided by the observable noise estimate sqrt(limit_counts^2 + max(counts, 0))

payload_columns.name: ra
payload_columns.measure: east offset Delta alpha cos(delta) of the planet from the star, flux-weighted over the science interval; 0 and unread unless detected = 1

payload_columns.name: dec
payload_columns.measure: north offset Delta delta of the planet from the star, flux-weighted over the science interval; 0 and unread unless detected = 1

payload_columns.name: ra_err
payload_columns.measure: standard deviation of ra, kappa (lambda/D) / snr

payload_columns.name: dec_err
payload_columns.measure: standard deviation of dec, kappa (lambda/D) / snr

payload_columns.name: corr
payload_columns.measure: correlation of the ra and dec errors

payload_columns.name: cadence
payload_columns.measure: detector cadence mode the row was computed with

payload_columns.name: calibration_id
payload_columns.measure: six-byte digest of the detector, cadence, optics, response, nominal scene and law declarations

payload_columns.name: valid_science
payload_columns.sign: flag: 1 science interval inside the certified window, 0 otherwise
payload_columns.measure: whether the visit produced a certified science interval

boundaries.name: geometry_position
boundaries.measure: maximum difference over three eccentricities by 64 epochs; signs at four phases; east offset with and without cos(delta)
boundaries.allocation: 0.29 mas total; Kepler solve 0.01 mas; phase angle 1e-9 rad
boundaries.reference: 30-digit Kepler solution and hand signs from a generator that imports no library under test

boundaries.name: geometry_contrast
boundaries.measure: superior conjunction, quadrature, near inferior conjunction
boundaries.reference: Lambert phase and the formula by hand, constants from astropy.constants

boundaries.name: time_epoch
boundaries.measure: exact tick to JD round trip; opposite relabelling; JD to MJD; midpoint formula

boundaries.name: time_keepout
boundaries.measure: orbix is_observable sampled every 6 hours over two years
boundaries.allocation: 70 d per yr, plus or minus 2 d, for a 45 degree Sun keepout at the target's ecliptic latitude
boundaries.reference: spherical trigonometry: half-width arccos(cos 45 deg / cos beta) in Sun longitude

boundaries.name: radiometry_planet_counts
boundaries.measure: constant planet; two bandwidths; time-averaged value on a moving planet
boundaries.reference: F0 10^(-0.4 m) contrast area throughput QE band time by hand, area pi (D/2)^2 (1 - OBSCURED)

boundaries.name: radiometry_zodi
boundaries.measure: dependence on ecliptic latitude and solar longitude across a year
boundaries.reference: the one-zodi surface-brightness definition by hand

boundaries.name: radiometry_exozodi
boundaries.measure: separation sweep in AU; aperture sweep; two hosts of different luminosity
boundaries.reference: 1 / r_AU^2 at fixed host, linear in aperture solid angle, L / Lsun factor, by hand

boundaries.name: radiometry_leakage
boundaries.measure: native 0.25 and rebinned 0.5 sampling; diameter 0 versus 0.03 lambda/D; annular-bin control fails
boundaries.reference: independent NumPy circle average of the cube about 127.5 divided by 0.25^2, times core area

boundaries.name: detector_variance
boundaries.measure: zero-noise and each-source-alone cases; sub-frame, exact-frame, n frames and n frames plus a partial last frame
boundaries.reference: N / sqrt(N + k B + D(t)) with D(t) written out
boundaries.status: blocked: jaxedith finite-duration fixed-frame variance API

boundaries.name: reporting_law
boundaries.observable: detection frequency, retained counts, astrometric covariance
boundaries.measure: 20000 draws at three signal levels with s(theta) != s0; corr = 0 and corr = 0.5; wrong-threshold control fails
boundaries.allocation: 3 Monte Carlo standard errors; Kolmogorov-Smirnov p above 0.01; whitened residual chi-square

boundaries.name: inference_calibration
boundaries.allocation: probability-integral-transform CDF inside the DKW band at 100 worlds (half-width 0.136); coverage inside a Bonferroni band
boundaries.reference: the truth value of each world
